title: Cooked, frozen, burnt
goal: Describe things with -mIş adjectives (pişmiş tavuk, donmuş göl), and tell a story that mixes what you saw and what you found out.

intro.text: `-mIş` also works as an adjective: *pişmiş tavuk* (cooked chicken), *donmuş göl* (a frozen lake), *kızarmış ekmek* (toast). One minibus even took its name from it: the *dolmuş*, which leaves once it has filled up.

exercises.question: *Ekmek yanmış!* and *yanmış ekmek*: which is a full sentence?

why.1: *Yanmış ekmek* is a phrase, **burnt bread**: `-mIş` describes the noun after it.

exercises.explain: After its noun, *yanmış* is the verb: **the bread has burnt!**

exercises.text: Kahvaltıda kızar___ ekmek ve peynir yedik.
exercises.en: We had toast and cheese for breakfast.

reject.why: *Kızardı* would be a verb, **it got toasted**. To describe the bread, use the adjective *kızarmış*.

accept: We walked on the frozen lake.

exercises.prompt: We went to Taksim by dolmuş.

exercises.tr: Masada pişmiş tavuk ve pilav vardı.
exercises.en: There was cooked chicken and rice on the table.

exercises.title: Komşunun kedisi
exercises.passage:
Dün akşam eve geldim. Kapının önünde küçük bir kedi vardı. Komşum Selin'e sordum: “Bu kedi kimin?” Selin bilmiyordu. Sonra kapıcıya sordum. Kedi üst kattaki yeni komşununmuş.

Bu sabah kedi yine kapımın önündeydi. Meğer yeni komşu bir haftalığına tatile gitmiş, kediye de kapıcı bakıyormuş.
exercises.translation: I came home yesterday evening. There was a little cat in front of the door. I asked my neighbour Selin: “Whose cat is this?” Selin didn't know. Then I asked the caretaker. The cat belonged to the new neighbour upstairs, it turned out. This morning the cat was in front of my door again. It turns out the new neighbour has gone on holiday for a week, and the caretaker is looking after the cat.

questions.q: Why does the second paragraph switch to *gitmiş* and *bakıyormuş*?
questions.explain: `-mIş` marks what the narrator learned second-hand: she didn't see the neighbour leave.

questions.q: Who is looking after the cat?
questions.explain: *Kediye kapıcı bakıyormuş*: `-(I)yor` + `-mIş`, **the caretaker is looking after it, it turns out**.

exercises.en: There were dried flowers in the vase.
exercises.explain: Before a noun, `-mIş` is an adjective: *kurumuş çiçekler*, **dried flowers**.

exercises.text: The past is in the past.
accept: The past stayed in the past.

exercises.question: A friend tells you: *Yarın otobüsler çalışmayacakmış.* What is she saying?
options: The buses won't run tomorrow, she heard.
She doesn't want to take the bus.
exercises.explain: *Çalışmayacakmış*: negative future + `-mIş`, passing on news. *Çalışmak* also means **to run, to work** for buses and machines.
